Sally Fenner meets Edith Lowy,
Managing Director of

First Lady

Edith Lowy is a woman who has succeeded in a man's world, not only in this country but also in the unfamiliar Middle East. As possibly the only woman managing director of a UK company manufacturing domestic electrical appliances, she heads a company which has a turnover of more than a million pounds a year, has a workforce of 25 plus, and has had a full order book throughout the recession period.

brief_context: Country mentioned in context of Edith Lowy's business travel.
article_title: First Lady of electric space heating
brief_extract: At that time, and indeed even now, it was not easy for a woman to make business deals in the male dominated Middle Eastern countries, and Edith would often find herself the only woman at a trade reception. In fact, she still cannot enter Saudi Arabia without a male escort. However, although warned that she would find it difficult to sell in these countries — and particularly to sell electric space heaters — she in fact found the local businessmen extremely helpful and pleasant.

brief_extract: Before Mr Smith joined us in 1975 he had spent 35 years in the travel industry, plus war service in the RAF. He had worked his way through the travel business from a pre-war counter clerk selling a single fare to New York on the Queen Mary for £18.10s, to General Manager of a chain of travel agencies in the 1960's and 70's. He saw a complete change within the travel industry, from the very male-dominated scene before the war to the current situation where women predominate.

Ernest Smith confesses to a fascination for facts and figures — a vital attribute to anyone in travel work where he was always alert for new information and, as he describes it, 'ferreting out' information for clients and for ways of extending the business.

article_title: ERNEST SMITH retires
brief_extract: "I regard my time on the staff of the EAW as being amongst my most enjoyable years," he told us. Ernest lives with his wife and son in Wimbledon, and has a married daughter living in Cheshire. He is not likely to be idle when he retires, or to lose touch with the Association, having agreed to make himself available for consultation if necessary.

article_title: ERNEST SMITH retires
brief_extract: He is also a keen cook and enjoys preparing and adapting recipes, and is always concerned to use only natural ingredients. His travel career added to this interest — the taste of paella on a trip to Spain would have him producing it for dinner as soon as he returned home. He even persuaded the men's club of the local chapel (perhaps against their initial inclination) to produce a very successful three-course hot meal for their wives.
